He took the safety precautions about the vehicles parking and placed the stones and camphire near the accident place. The accident occurred due to negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus driver only. Hence the Respondent no.3 and 4 not liable to pay any compensation to the Petitioner. Further Respondents denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by him and disability caused to him and also contended that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.

10. On basis of the Pleadings and materials, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that, on 03.10.2022 at about 01.45 am, the petitioner was travelling as a commuter in a KSRTC Bus bearing No. KA-57-F-3

when he reached Hoskote Mylapura Gate, at that time all of sudden he raised the speed of the said Bus and lost the control over his vehicle and dashed against Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16-D-9498 parking the vehicle in left of the road without

As a result of forced impact,
petitioner sustained grievous injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. Whether order or award?
Heard the arguments and Perused the materials available on record.

On perusal of Spot sketch and Charge sheet it appears that, near Mylapura Gate Hosakote,
opposite to NH - 75 Hotel, Bangalore driver of 11 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 KSRTC bus bearing Reg. No.KA-57/F-3773 drove the same in a rash and negligent

5 parked on the road by its driver without any precautionary measures.
Further IMV report discloses that, the rear portion of the Lorry and front portion of the KSRTC bus were damaged.

Hence,
Hosakote Police filed Charge sheet against driver of the KSRTC Bus as A1 and driver of Lorry as A2.

22 . In the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the claimant has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required as held by t

The so-called reason that as the name of Dheeraj Kumar was not mentioned in the FIR, so it was not possible for Dheeraj Kumar to see the incident, is not a proper assessment of the fact-situation in this case.
It is well known that in a case relating to motor accident claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as it is required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Court must keep this distinction in mind.

Reference in this connection may be made to the decision of this Court in Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others (2009) 13 SCC 530, in which the relevant observation on this point has been made and which is
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touch stone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
23. After careful scrutiny of Ex.P1 - F.I.R., Ex.P2 - Complaint.
Ex.P3 - Spot sketch, Ex.P4 - Spot Mahazar, Ex.P5 - IMV report, Ex.P6 - Wound certificate and Ex.P7 Charge sheet

it appears that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773 and also due to negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498.
Accordingly, I answer the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

Hence, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, the Petitioner is entitled for amount of Rs.80,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
25. The Petitioner had not produced even a single medical bill.
However he had produced two discharge summary which are marked as Ex.P8 and 9.
As per Ex,P8 the Petitioner took treatment at Jayanagar Orthopaedic Centre from 03-10-2022 to 08-10-2022.
Ex,P8 discloses that, the Petitioner took treatment at MVJ Hospital from 03-10-2022 to 03-10-2022.

Therefore, by considering the period of treatment taken as inpatient this tribunal awarded reasonable compensation of Rs.8,000/-
under the head Medical expenses, Transportation, food, Nourishment and conveyance charges.
To prove the assessment of disability, the Petitioner got examined one Doctor Shri.Somashekar as Pw-3.

In the chief examination affidavit the doctor deposed that, on examination it is found that,
the Petitioner walks with pain and limping, Diffuse swelling of left lower limb and Surgical scars are seen over left knee, leg and ankle.
Recent X-ray shows that United fracture of both bones of left leg with implants in situ as both sites.

The doctor assessed the total disability of left lower limb at 42%
and that of to the whole body of the Petitioner at 21%.
In the Cross examination doctor had deposed that, " I am not a treated doctor at any stage.
It is true to suggest that, fractures are united as per recent x-rays.
It is true to suggest that, there is no bone loss and no shortening limb.
It is true to suggest that, as per guidelines 50% of disability of particulars limb cannot taken towards the whole body."
However by considering the nature of the injury and evidence of the doctor, this Tribunal had taken the disability of the Petitioner at 15% to the whole body.

27. It is contended that prior to the accident, the Petitioner was Painter by Profession and was 15 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 earning Rs.25,000/- p.m and due to accidental injuries he is not able to carry on his work as before the accident.
The Petitioner had not produced any document to prove his income and avocation.
In present days the Coolie worker get Rs.500/- to 600/- per day.
However by considering the age and occupation of petitioner this Tribunal taken the monthly income of the Petitioner at Rs.16,000/-.
28. As per Ex.P10 Notarized Copy of Aadhaar card date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 30- 07-1981.
Therefore, age of the Petitioner is taken as 41 years at the time of accident.

Then the proper multiplier applicable is 14 which comes as follows:
Rs.16,000 x 12 x 14 x 15% = Rs.4,03,200/- Hence, I award Rs.4,03,200/- under the head loss of future earning capacity on account of disability.
29.
Towards future medication the Doctor deposed in his chief examination affidavit that, the Petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants at both sides which would cost around Rs.40,000/-.

30. The Petitioner was Painter profession and due to accidental injuries his routine work was hampered for some days.

33. Liability:-
The Respondent No.1 is the RC owner-cum- Insurer of KSRTC bus bearing Reg No.KA-57/F- 37

Respondent No.2 is the Insurer, Respondent No.3 is the owner and as per the Charge sheet the Respondent No.4 is the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498.

In the Written statement the respondent No.1 KSRTC contended that, they had paid a sum of Rs.11,356/- to the Petitioner on humanitarian ground without admitting the liability.
But the respondent No.1 had not produced any document 18 SCCH - 19 MVC.7057/2022 to prove that they had paid the amount of Rs.11,356/- to the Petitioner.
Hence, the said amount cannot be deducted out of total compensation amount.

As already discussed in the issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus driver and also due to negligence in parking of Lorry by it's driver jointly and severally liable to pay comp

Further, the Respondent No.1 is being RC Owner-cum-Insurer of the KSRTC Bus and Respondent No.2 being Insurer of the Lorry are primarily held liable to pay the 50% each of the compensation amount with interest to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.

36. Issue No.3: for the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act filed by the Petitioners is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,31,200/- (Rupees five lakh, thirty one thousand and two hundred only) with interest @ 6% p.a., (excluding future medical expenses) from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay aforesaid compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Petition against Respondent No.4 (i.e., driver of offending vehicle) is hereby dismissed.

Out of total compensation amount, the Respondent No.1 is being owner of KSRTC bus and the Respondent No.2 being Insurer of the Lorry are directed to deposit 50% each together with 6%
interest p.a. within 60 days, from the date of this Orde
